texts: One dance, 52 joints, any humanoid skeleton: how three.ws retargets motion to rigs from other tools

One 9.87 second dance clip, authored once on a 52-joint skeleton, now plays in step on Mixamo-prefixed, unprefixed and other avatars it was not made for. The write-up shows how bone names are matched, why a matching name is not enough, and where the retargeter refuses: three.ws/rig-doctor

issues.problem: The results table asserts specific joint and track counts for six avatar files (65, 67, 52, 38, 36, 24 joints; 36 canonical; 37 of 53 tracks), and the article claims "I ran every line of this against the current source" and "Run it as node coverage.mjs ... and it prints the same rows as the table." No verification entry covers these per-file numbers, the avatar filenames (michelle.glb, dancing-twerk.glb, studio.glb, cz.glb, realistic-halfbody.glb, fox.glb), or the statements that the leftover joints are "fingertip, toe and head-top end bones, which no clip animates." The run evidence only probes the Rig Doctor against a Mixamo sample, not this table.
issues.fix: Run the coverage script in the article against the six files in the repo's avatars folder and record the output as verification, or have the article state the numbers it actually prints. If the files cannot be run, cut the per-file counts to what is verified (52 canonical joints, 53 retargetable tracks, the Mixamo-prefix stripping) and describe the fox and half-body outcomes qualitatively with evidence.

issues.quote: its Vertex AI integration lets agents leverage Gemini models
issues.problem: "Leverage" is filler register, already flagged by the mechanical check; the partners page wording exists, so use plain language or the exact page phrasing.
issues.fix: Replace with "its Vertex AI integration lets agents use Gemini models alongside the three.ws identity layer."

issues.quote: The leftovers are the fingertip end bones and the toe and head-top end bones, which no clip animates.
issues.problem: Specific claim about which joints Rig Doctor lists as unrecognized for michelle.glb has no evidence entry.
issues.fix: Capture the Rig Doctor output for michelle.glb and quote the unrecognized list, or soften to "the leftover end bones, which no clip animates" only if the evidence shows it.

issues.quote: A man in a pink tailcoat, a green felt hat and a plum bow tie, caught mid-dance against a dark background with his fists raised at his chest.
issues.problem: The article lead promises four dancers in step, but the cover shows one avatar; the inline four-rig images carry that claim, so the cover undersells the headline and centers on vast empty black space that will crop with heavy dead margins in the timeline.
issues.fix: Use the four-rigs-one-dance-a.png frame as the cover so the image matches the title's "one dance ... any humanoid skeleton" claim, or recapture the single-avatar shot framed tighter.
